_**User**_

In Next.js when you have to crate a link to another page that isn't the one you already at, I mean to another domain (to an entire new page) you should use <Link> o <a>?

---

_**Agent (composer-1.5)**_

For links to another domain, use a plain HTML `<a>` tag, not Next.js `<Link>`.

**Why:**

1. **`<Link>` is for internal routes** – It’s meant for same-origin navigation and client-side routing. External URLs don’t benefit from that.

2. **Prefetching** – `<Link>` prefetches routes by default. That doesn’t apply to external sites and can be wasteful or unwanted.

3. **Security** – External links usually need `target="_blank"` and `rel="noopener noreferrer"`, which you add on `<a>`.

**Example:**

```tsx
// External link — use <a>
<a
  href="https://example.com"
  target="_blank"
  rel="noopener noreferrer"
>
  Visit Example
</a>

// Internal link — use <Link>
<Link href="/about">About</Link>
```

**Rule of thumb:** Use `<Link>` for same-origin routes (e.g. `/about`, `/projects`), and `<a>` for external URLs.
